sentences.text: Taohelong possessed a sacral shield, which is a carpet of osteoderms covering the hips similar to those found in other ankylosaurians.
The osteoderms making up Taohelong's sacral shield are irregular in both their shape and size.
The neural channel of Taohelong's tail vertebra has a cross-section shaped like an inverted trapezium.
The outer rim of Taohelong's ilium has a profile resembling a mirrored 'S' when viewed from the top.
Taohelong was named and described in 2013 by Yang Jing-Tao, You Hai-Lu, Li Da-Qing, and Kong De-Lai.
The only known fossil of Taohelong was discovered in the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin near the border of Yongjing and Lintao counties by the Gansu Zhendan Dinosaur Culture Communication Company.
The holotype specimen GSDM 00021 was described in 2013 by Yang Jingtao, You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Kong Delai as the new ankylosaur taxon Taohelong jinchengensis.
The genus name Taohelong refers to the Tao River, while the species name jinchengensis references the ancient name of Lanzhou, Jincheng, meaning 'solid' to describe the animal's armor.
Taohelong is classified within the family Nodosauridae, specifically in the subfamily Polacanthinae.
Phylogenetic analysis identifies Taohelong as the sister taxon to Polacanthus foxii, making it the first described polacanthine from Asia.
Taohelong jinchengensis lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 110 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
Taohelon lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, spanning from 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago.
A sauropod distinct from Huanghetitan and Daxiatitan was found 200 meters away from the Taohelong fossil site within the Hekou Group.
